context: Build a GitHub repository called code-conductor in the current directory. This is a structured, token-efficient agent for Claude Code. All design decisions are final. Generate every file complete and immediately usable. No placeholders. No truncation. No confirmation between files unless explicitly stated.
architecture: Three layers: 1. Global core → ~/.claude/ — applies to every project on the machine 2. Project template → project root — versioned in git, shared with the team 3. Stack profiles + skills — loaded dynamically based on detected stack
file_structure: code-conductor/ ├── README.md ├── .gitignore ├── install.sh macOS/Linux — works with: curl -fsSL URL | bash ├── install.ps1 Windows — works with: irm URL | iex ├── global/ │ ├── CLAUDE.md Global core. Applies to ALL projects. │ ├── settings.json │ ├── commands/ │ │ ├── checkpoint.md /checkpoint │ │ ├── stack.md /stack │ │ └── lang.md /lang │ └── memory/ │ └── personal.md Template. Never committed to git. ├── project-template/ │ ├── CLAUDE.md Extends global. Project-specific overrides. │ └── .claude/ │ ├── settings.json │ ├── commands/ │ │ ├── spec.md /spec │ │ ├── plan.md /plan │ │ ├── review.md /review │ │ ├── debug.md /debug — includes Playwright MCP │ │ ├── refactor.md /refactor │ │ ├── test.md /test — includes Playwright E2E │ │ └── docs.md /docs │ ├── hooks/ │ │ ├── pre-tool-use.sh Blocks duplicate file creation │ │ └── post-compact.sh Reminds to checkpoint after /compact │ └── memory/ │ └── project.md Shared team memory. In git. ├── stack-profiles/ │ ├── _base.md │ ├── _multi-stack.md │ ├── _template.md │ ├── javascript.md │ ├── typescript.md │ ├── python.md │ ├── java.md │ ├── go.md │ ├── rust.md │ ├── react.md │ ├── angular.md │ ├── nextjs.md │ ├── nestjs.md │ ├── django.md │ └── flask.md └── skills/ ├── code-simplifier.md Always active. Loaded by global core. └── ui-ux.md Activatable for frontend projects.
agent_behaviors:
MANDATORY — encode these in global/CLAUDE.md:
- WORKFLOW: /spec → /plan → confirm → implement. No code without approved spec. - TOKENS: grep/find before read. Never read full file over 150 lines. One tool call, one purpose. - SAFETY: check file exists before create. Confirm before any write or destructive command. - SIMPLICITY: code-simplifier always active. No speculative abstractions. No premature patterns. - LANGUAGE: English by default. /lang [code] switches session. Code identifiers always English. - STACK: auto-run /stack at session start. Confirm before loading profiles. - MEMORY: project.md in git (shared). personal.md local only (never committed). - DELEGATION: Superpowers for isolated tasks. Playwright for visual debug and E2E. - RESPONSE FORMATS: [CHANGES], [BUG], [PLAN], [REASON] — always use these tags.
installers:
Both install.sh and install.ps1 must have identical behavior, different syntax. Use REPO="YOUR_ORG/code-conductor" variable at top of both files.
Order: Node.js 18+ (primary) → Python 3 (secondary) → error + exit if neither. If Node missing: auto-install via Homebrew (macOS) → nvm (macOS/Linux) → apt/dnf/pacman (Linux) → winget (Windows). If auto-install fails and Python also missing: print clear error listing what to install, exit 1.
Install in this order. On failure: warn, continue, report at end.
1. claude-mem command: npx claude-mem install requires: Node 18+
2. ui-ux-pro-max-skill command: npm install -g uipro-cli && uipro init --ai claude --global requires: Node + Python 3
3. Playwright MCP command: claude mcp add playwright npx @playwright/mcp@latest requires: Node + claude CLI
4. Superpowers command: claude plugin install superpowers@claude-plugins-official requires: claude CLI
5. code-simplifier command: claude plugin install code-simplifier@claude-plugins-official requires: claude CLI
User-configured files (skip if exist): CLAUDE.md, settings.json, memory templates Agent-managed files (always overwrite): commands, hooks, stack profiles, skills Source: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/${REPO}/${BRANCH}/[path]
--project / -Project → also install project template into current directory → update .gitignore to exclude .claude/memory/personal.md --no-deps → skip dependency installation, agent files only
Show: what installed, what failed with manual commands, available slash commands.
commands_spec:
/checkpoint Read recent conversation. Identify: decisions, conventions, debt, workarounds. Update project.md (append, never delete). Update personal.md with dev preferences. Report with timestamp: what was saved in each file. Suggest automatically: before /compact, after feature completion, after key decisions.
/stack Scan: package.json, pom.xml, build.gradle, go.mod, requirements.txt, pyproject.toml, Cargo.toml, *.csproj, composer.json, Gemfile, pubspec.yaml. Infer framework from dependency contents, not just file existence. If multi-language: load _multi-stack.md as coordinator first. If stack in project.md memory: load from there, ask if anything changed. Confirm before loading profiles.
/lang [code] Switch immediately. Confirm in the new language. Scope: responses + code comments. Never: identifiers, file names, commits. Without argument: show current state + available codes (en es pt fr de it zh ja ko). Hierarchy: session (/lang) > project CLAUDE.md > personal.md > default English.
/spec [name] Search codebase for related existing code before asking questions. Ask only missing context: problem, user, constraints, existing similar features. Generate: problem, solution, behavior (main/alternative/error cases), acceptance criteria, out of scope, system impact, complexity estimate. Wait for explicit approval. Save summary to project.md. Do not proceed to /plan without approval.
/plan Require approved spec. Read project CLAUDE.md and project.md memory. Map codebase structure before reading any file content. Generate: ordered steps with exact file paths and actions, test list, commit order, identified risks, step dependencies. Execute one step at a time. Confirm between steps unless dev says otherwise.
/review [file|dir|nothing] No input → git diff HEAD. Layers: 🔴 Critical (blocks merge), 🟡 Important (must fix), 🟢 Suggestion. Critical: bugs, security, data loss, breaking changes. Important: error handling, missing tests, convention violations, N+1 queries. Verdict: APPROVED | APPROVED WITH CHANGES | BLOCKED. Offer to auto-fix critical+important after report.
/debug [problem] Characterize: symptom, expected, reproduction, frequency, context. List 2-4 hypotheses by probability. Confirm before investigating. Activate Playwright MCP for visual bugs or UI flow issues. Produce: root cause, location (file:line), impact, proposed fix. Apply fix only after confirmation. Suggest test if bug was non-obvious.
/refactor [file|module] Diagnose: complexity issues with line references. Plan: ordered changes with what/why/risk per step. Execute one change at a time. Verify tests after each step. Report: before/after line count, delta, test status.
/test [scope] Analyze coverage gaps first. Define strategy (unit/integration/E2E). AAA pattern for all tests. Language-specific runners. E2E with Playwright: confirm app is running, navigate, interact, capture, generate test. Run after confirmation. Report: passed/failed/skipped + coverage if available.
/docs [scope] Audit existing docs first. Prioritize public APIs and core modules. Inline format by language: JSDoc (JS/TS), docstrings (Python), JavaDoc (Java), GoDoc (Go). Document WHY not WHAT. Preview before writing to files.
hooks_spec:
pre-tool-use.sh Trigger: Write, Create, write_file, create_file tool calls. Extract file path from CLAUDE_TOOL_INPUT JSON. If file exists: print warning (path, line count, last modified), list 3 options, exit 1. If path not extractable: exit 0 (do not block on hook error).
post-compact.sh Read project.md, show last checkpoint timestamp. Print reminder to run /checkpoint if session had important decisions.
stack_profiles_spec:
Each profile defines: - Naming conventions table (variables, functions, classes, constants, files, dirs) - Standard project structure - Tooling table (formatter, linter, test runner, build tool, package manager) - Common commands (install, dev, test, build, format, lint) - 2-3 idiomatic patterns with examples - Anti-patterns to avoid - Detector files list
_base.md: English identifiers always, Conventional Commits in English, one file one responsibility, no silent error swallowing, never hardcode secrets, comments explain why not what.
_multi-stack.md: each layer owns its directory, cross-layer contracts are source of truth, language-specific tools stay in their layer, full-stack feature order (contract → backend → frontend → tests → E2E).
Generate with real idiomatic conventions. No generic filler.
skills_spec:
skills/code-simplifier.md — ALWAYS ACTIVE Rules with code examples (good vs bad) for: - No speculative abstractions (solve today's problem) - No premature layers (add only when layer carries real logic) - No single-implementation interfaces - Functions do one thing (max 30 lines) - No defensive code for impossible cases - No design patterns by default - Flat over nested (guard clauses, early return) - Descriptive names (no Base/Abstract/Generic/Manager/Handler) - Constants only when used 2+ places or have domain meaning - Comments explain why, never what
Complexity signals (stop and simplify): class with 5+ deps, function over 30 lines, 3+ nesting levels, layer that only delegates, name with Base/Abstract/Generic.
When complexity IS justified: multiple real implementations today, domain rules are genuinely complex, performance constraint with documented reason, pattern prevents a bug class that already occurred.
skills/ui-ux.md — ACTIVATABLE Design principles: visual hierarchy, whitespace as signal, consistency system, motion with purpose. Component approach: identify hierarchy → states → variants before writing. Required states: default, hover/focus, active, disabled, loading, error, empty. Typography scale, spacing scale (4px base), semantic color tokens. Patterns: cards, forms, tables, navigation, toast/alert feedback. Anti-patterns: flat gray cards, uniform buttons, no hover states, color for decoration, modal for everything. Accessibility baseline: contrast ratios, keyboard nav, focus indicators, alt text, label associations. Tailwind conventions: design tokens, group/peer, gap over margin, dark: variants.
readme_spec: Structure: 1. Title + one-line description 2. Install section — one-liners PROMINENTLY at top, both OS 3. Add to project — one-liners with flags 4. Update — re-run same one-liner 5. What this solves — table: problem | solution 6. Available commands — two tables: global | project 7. Language support — 3-level hierarchy table + supported codes 8. Stack profiles — table 9. Memory architecture — text diagram 10. Full file structure 11. .gitignore note
